round_1.summary: The units conclusion reproduces. On a fresh seed (20261103), 4 random subjects not drawn by the worker (AB05, AB12, AB13, AB06; 6 legs) plus a targeted AB03 check (2 new tasks, 4 legs) were tested. A mass-free lever-arm ankle moment in N·m maps onto the source column with an implied mass of 67-120 kg (never about 1 kg); correlation is at least 0.9875. A second fit with a free talus point gives 62-117 kg and recovers a plausible talus point (x 0.047-0.059 m). Plate-derived body masses match the README within 4 %. Powers equal moment times velocity in rad/s. ProcessedData moments are identical to RawData. My code reproduces the worker's AB02 numbers. Returned for sheet rule fixes (text under 10 pt, a task ID in the reply line) and a future handoff timestamp. Two findings are recorded for later work: the AB03 denominator and the AB05 scale anomaly. No scientific approval is implied.

Drawn: AB05 incline_walk_2, AB12 weighted_walk_1, AB13 incline_walk_1, AB06 weighted_walk_1; 0 redraws. AB12 and AB06 have no right plate (README note). Talus point from each trial's own model (Statics.csv -> <subj>-Scaled<n>.osim subtalar location_in_parent). It equals the generic (0.04877, 0.04195) m in every model parsed. Fixed lever, 40-90 % stance: implied mass AB05 115.3/120.4, AB12 67.6, AB13 67.2/68.1, AB06 74.6 kg (README 71.5, 64.0, 67.6, 79.1); correlation 0.9875-0.9999. checks.name: Free-lever fit (new)
checks.evidence: source = b1*(-cop_x*Fy) + b2*(-Fx) + b3*Fy over 20-90 % stance, so that the mass and the talus point are fitted together: implied mass AB05 113.9/117.1, AB12 66.4, AB13 65.7/62.5, AB06 71.6, AB03 81.7/77.9/85.4/81.7 kg; talus x 0.047-0.059 m, y 0.045-0.076 m; R^2 0.992-0.9999. The talus point it recovers is anatomically plausible, so the per-kg scale is not an artifact of the assumed ankle position.

checks.name: Plate-derived body mass

findings_for_later_work: AB03 denominator: in 2 new tasks (normal_walk_1 with model Scaled1, incline_walk_1 with model Scaled4), 4 legs, the implied normalizing mass is 83-85 kg (fixed lever) and 78-85 kg (free lever). This agrees with the worker's weighted_walk_1 (85.7). AB03's own models all weigh 113.517 kg and the plates give 111-115 kg. AB03/Models also holds AB02-Scaled1.osim (82.179 kg), and that file is where the local Subject_masses.csv got its AB03 value of 82.18. The source AB03 moments therefore look as if they were divided by about 82 kg, not 113.5, which would make them about 38 % too large per kg. This is suggestive, not conclusive: other single trials also stray (AB05 incline_walk_2 implies 114-120 kg against 71.5, and the worker's AB10 incline_walk_1 1.3x and AB08 weighted 0.73x), so trial-level scale anomalies exist beyond AB03. The 3 of 4 clean new subjects agree with the README within 6 %. A José exclusion or correction decision may follow once a cause is found.
The converters normalize GRF by the local RawData/Subject_masses.csv, so AB03 body-weight GRF would be about 38 % too high. The worker already notes that the publisher mass table must be used.
